claim: A strategy with no edge passes the 60%-of-years rule 36-38% of the time over 8-10 years
ours: true Sharpe 0, 15% vol: 28% / 30% (iid), 29% / 31% (KOSPI sign-flip), 24% / 24% (KOSPI bootstrap); 12 y 13%, 20 y 16% (iid)
reason: 36-38% is the binomial value for P(year > 0) = 0.5, i.e. a zero MEDIAN year (Sharpe about +0.075 at 15% vol). At zero Sharpe the compounding drag gives P(year > 0) = 0.47 (lognormal formula 30% / 31%), and KOSPI-like volatility clustering lowers it further. The rate also jumps with the year count (rounding of 60%).
